correctness.rationale: The Gaussian Markov bridge and extrapolation conditional variances integrate exactly to H(d)=d coth d-1 and G(a)=a-(1-e^{-2a})/2. Both component costs are strictly convex on nonnegative gaps with zero derivative at zero; the unique optimal simplex point is interior. Lagrange equations and monotonic derivatives force equal interiors and equal margins. An explicit strictly positive derivative gap proves margins strictly shorter. Taylor and large-gap expansions justify both asymptotic regimes. Independent matrix-based Gaussian variance integration and 1,192 reproducibility assertions pass; finite tests are not used as the proof.

originality.rationale: Closest inspected source on identical OU covariance and IMSPE (Dasgupta et al., Theorem 5.2) explicitly fixes both observations at the transect endpoints; its equal-gap result is not an optimizer for free endpoints. Zimmerman addresses geostatistical design, largely by numerical finite grids with different mean assumptions. published-finding corpus OU Bayesian quadrature has different loss (variance of integral rather than integral of variance) and opposite terminal margin ordering. This claim remains priority-provisional because the full 2010 exact-design paper was inaccessible; the access limitation does not amount to evidence of coverage.
residual_risks: A direct full-text comparison against Antognini and Zagoraiou (2010), DOI 10.1016/j.jspi.2010.03.027, could not be completed; its abstract and secondary descriptions do not decide whether it contains a free-terminal exact theorem.
General optimal Gaussian process design treatises or unindexed exact free-endpoint optimization may establish a mathematically equivalent theorem; semantic absence is not a novelty proof.
The close OU Bayesian quadrature literature has superficially similar optimal-gap equations, but its statistical target is inequivalent.

value.rationale: The exact continuous optimum resolves whether environmental monitoring stations should be placed at domain boundaries or shifted inward under simple kriging. The derived universal short-transect 1:3 edge-to-inner law, long-transect logarithmic correction, and unique scalar parameterization provide a full station-count and correlation-scale phase-free design prescription. For two stations at theta L=1 it lowers integrated model prediction variance by 40.44 percent relative to compulsory boundary stations, a substantial motivated effect of choosing the correct feasible design rather than a mere algebraic relabeling. Not presented as field advice without model validation.
